paragraphs: Hello! I'm Durjoy, a passionate cybersecurity researcher with expertise in protecting digital infrastructures and identifying security vulnerabilities. My journey spans from practical security operations to academic research in AI security and cryptography.

My research journey began during my sophomore year of graduation, evolving from a fascination with system vulnerabilities into focused investigation of AI-driven security threats and quantum-safe cryptographic systems. Through hands-on experience and rigorous academic exploration, I've developed a deep understanding of both offensive and defensive security paradigms.

Driven by an insatiable curiosity and a mission to fortify digital landscapes, I approach cybersecurity as more than a technical discipline—it's a continuous journey of anticipating, understanding, and neutralizing emerging threats. My passion lies not just in mastering tools and techniques, but in cultivating a proactive, adaptive mindset that bridges theoretical research with practical implementation.

Currently, I'm a Junior Research Associate at Security Lab @ IIT Patna, working on Blockchain and distributed systems security. My work focuses on developing practical solutions to emerging security challenges while contributing to academic literature.
I am actively seeking research or internship opportunities to advance my expertise in the field and contribute toward making the world safer bit by bit.

researchInterests.title: Research Focus
researchInterests.statement: My research interests focus on the security of distributed and blockchain systems. I am interested in understanding how these systems behave under realistic adversarial conditions, and in exploring practical ways to evaluate and improve security, trust, and reliability through experimentation and system-level analysis.

research.title: Beyond Copy–Pasting—Contextualizing LLMs for Secure Code Generation
research.description: This study evaluates security vulnerabilities in code generated by Large Language Models (LLMs) and co-pilots, emphasizing the need for strategic contextualization in Secure Coding Practices (SCPs). Through qualitative analysis, it assesses risks and proposes actionable strategies to help developers fine-tune LLMs for secure code generation. By integrating proactive security measures, this research aligns accelerated development with robust security practices.

research.title: Beyond Text: Nefarious Actors Harnessing LLMs for Strategic Advantage
research.description: This study explores how malicious actors exploit Large Language Models (LLMs) for cyber threats beyond conventional uses. Through literature review, case studies, and real-world analysis, it examines LLM-driven deception, social engineering, and cybercrimes like phishing, password cracking, and malware propagation, highlighting emerging security challenges.

research.title: Shadow APR-ing for APR Poisoning Detection
research.description: This study addresses ARP spoofing, a longstanding network security threat enabling attacks like MITM and DDoS. It proposes an automated OS-based monitoring technique to detect ARP poisoning in real time, reducing reliance on manual ARP table checks and minimizing detection delays.

scratchpad.intro: Not every experiment works out — and that's fine. Here's a graveyard of half-baked ideas, abandoned rabbit holes, and things I learned the hard way.

items.title: Custom Packet Sniffer in Rust
items.description: Tried building a raw packet sniffer entirely in Rust with zero dependencies. Got deep into raw sockets and AF_PACKET but hit platform portability walls.
items.lesson: Sometimes libpcap exists for a reason. Reinventing the wheel taught me a lot about the kernel networking stack though.

items.title: ML-based Malware Classifier from Syscalls
items.description: Hooked syscalls from sandboxed binaries and tried feeding sequences into an LSTM for behavioral classification. Accuracy plateaued at ~72%.
items.lesson: Feature engineering > model complexity. Syscall n-grams helped more than raw sequences. Might revisit with transformers.

items.title: Decentralized CTF Platform on IPFS
items.description: Wanted to host CTF challenges on IPFS so they'd be censorship-resistant. Turned out challenge isolation and scoring are fundamentally hard without a central server.
items.lesson: Decentralization is cool until you need state management and real-time scoring.

items.title: Browser Extension for Live CVE Alerts
items.description: A browser extension that cross-references the tech stack of the page you're visiting with NVD/CVE databases and shows active vulnerabilities. WIP.
items.lesson: Fingerprinting tech stacks client-side is messier than expected. Wappalyzer's approach is heavier than I thought.
